description: SCV hooks. Two kinds, and the distinction is the contract: the journal capture on UserPromptSubmit/Stop and the resume recap on SessionStart are non-blocking by design (the templates exit 0 on every failure and write nothing outside scv/journal/ — the SessionStart template writes nothing at all — with redaction running before anything hits disk or stdout; SessionStart is registered for compact|clear|resume only, never startup, because the first prompt's preflight already carries the project state there, Core 0.47.0+), while the PreToolUse guard is deliberately blocking — it denies writes no SCV action accounts for. The guard fails open on internal error and is inert in projects that have not adopted SCV. See vendor/scv-core/core/contracts/guard.md. The PostToolUse entry (Core 0.65.0+) is non-blocking too: after the user answers the choice tool, it records that the turn's registration predates the answer, so the guard asks for a fresh registration before the next write. The second PostToolUse entry (Core 0.79.0+, every tool) runs on-lang-check.sh: with SCV_LANG=korean it adds one correction line when text written since the last check drifted into another language; it never blocks. The PreToolUse entry with no matcher (Core 0.80.0+) runs the guard in gate-any mode: in a person's turn every tool except the help call itself and the SCV_HELP_FIRST_ALLOW list is refused until help has been called (Rule H). The same entry names the desktop app's wrap-up tool and its question field in SCV_SUMMARY_ASK (Core 0.102.0+, Rule S): a wrap-up call that carries a question is refused so the decision goes through AskUserQuestion first — before the closing text, so the choice is never shown late. Rule W (Core 0.104.0+) rides the same entry and needs no extra names, because the guard's default fields are Claude Code's own: a call whose wait_for_output_ms is 60 seconds or more (the desktop app's terminal-read tool), or a Bash command without run_in_background that sleeps 30 seconds or more or sleeps inside an until/while loop, is refused before it runs — the work goes to the background and the result is read when the notice comes, so a new message from the user does not cut the work off. Off: project setting SCV_BACKGROUND_FIRST=off.
